claims.text: Chemical short-range order governs the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of as-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy-alloy films or nanoribbons.
Lattice strain governs the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of these alloys.
Interface effects govern the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of these alloys.
Controlled annealing modifies chemical short-range order in these alloys.
Controlled annealing modifies lattice strain in these alloys.
Annealing-induced changes in chemical short-range order and lattice strain alter magnetic anisotropy.
Annealing-induced changes in chemical short-range order and lattice strain alter domain-wall dynamics.
Changes in magnetic anisotropy and domain-wall dynamics affect magnetocaloric response and hysteresis.
Annealing is expected to improve the magnetocaloric response relative to the as-deposited state.
Annealing is expected to reduce hysteresis relative to the as-deposited state.
The proposed operating-temperature range is 100–500 K.
The proposed magnetic-field range is 0–10 kOe.
Heat-transfer rate limits the magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify low-applied-field cycling, while the stated range extends to 10 kOe (approximately 1 T) without defining what portion qualifies as low field.
